extracted.intended_audience: exchange members, market participants, and SEC staff reviewing/non-transaction fee rule filings
extracted.subtask_description: A self-regulatory organization (exchange) rule filing proposing new or amended non-transaction fees (connectivity and port fees), including cost analyses, competitive/burden-on-competition discussion, and solicitation of public comment under the Exchange Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allocation methodology / no double-counting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange did not allocate any of its expenses in full to any core services (including physical connectivity or Limited Service MEI Ports) and did not double-count any expenses; instead it allocated applicable cost drivers across its core services and used the same Cost Analysis to form the basis of this proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate expenses across core services using appropriate cost drivers; avoid allocating an entire expense to a single service or double-counting the same expense across services. Use a single consistent Cost Analysis across related filings (e.g., connectivity and market data) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources cost allocation by function
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate personnel costs based on employees' functional focus (e.g., network infrastructure personnel allocated a high percentage to network infrastructure; smaller percentages allocated to Limited Service MEI Ports and other services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: network infrastructure personnel were allocated 42.4% to network infrastructure work, 8.0% to Limited Service MEI Ports, and the remainder to other services. Allocate smaller percentages across a broader set of personnel groups when tasks necessary to a service are not primary or full-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation & amortization allocation to connectivity services
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate depreciation and amortization expense to connectivity services to reflect computer equipment and network infrastructure used to operate the network, but not allocate all depreciation to connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example allocation: approx. 67.5% of overall depreciation/amortization to connectivity services (63.8% to 10Gb ULL and 3.7% to Limited Service MEI Ports), with the remainder allocated to transaction services, membership services, other port services and market data. Justify allocations by referencing the equipment and infrastructure that enable services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of observed usage data to set allocation percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation percentages should correspond with the number of applicable ports or other utilization metrics used on each exchange (e.g., port counts, matching engines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: differing allocations between exchanges were explained by different counts of ports utilized in August 2023 (e.g., 1,781 Limited Service MEI ports on MIAX vs. 1,030 on MIAX Emerald; MIAX Pearl Options used 384 Full Service MEO Ports). Use concrete usage counts to explain allocation differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate per-port cost calculation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute approximate cost per Limited Service MEI Port per month by dividing total monthly cost allocated to those ports by the total number of Limited Service MEI Ports utilized in the period, and include both free and charged ports in the denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: total monthly cost $148,255 / 1,030 ports = approx. $144 per port per month. Note prior filings may have omitted the expense of maintaining free ports when discussing per-port costs; be explicit about whether free ports' costs were included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee structure (free ports and per-port charge caps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed fee structure: provide a specified number of free Limited Service MEI Ports per matching engine (now four free per matching engine) and charge a set monthly fee for additional ports up to a stated maximum number per matching engine (charge $420 per Limited Service MEI Port per matching engine, up to 14 per engine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include worked examples to illustrate how free ports and charged ports interact across multiple matching engines (e.g., 12 matching engines × 14 ports = 168 ports; 4 free per engine = 48 free; 120 charged).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base cost analysis time frame and projection caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Base the Cost Analysis on a recent fiscal year (here, 2023 fiscal year operations) and express that actual costs may be higher or lower than projected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge uncertainty and that projections are estimates; disclose the time period used and the potential for variance between projections and actuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to periodic review and adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to conduct a one-year review after implementation and periodic reviews thereafter; if revenues fail to cover costs (plus reasonable mark-up) propose fee increases, and if revenues materially exceed projections propose fee decreases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing fee changes, include the results of timely reviews and updated cost estimates in any subsequent rule filing supporting the fee change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projected revenue and profit margin disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide projected annual costs, projected annual revenue, and the resulting estimated profit margin for each service (e.g., 10Gb ULL: cost $11,361,586 vs revenue $16,524,000 → 31% profit; Limited Service MEI Ports: cost $1,779,066 vs revenue $2,832,480 → 37% profit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use current usage data and the proposed fee schedule when producing projections and explicitly state the profit margin and note it may change over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking against affiliates and competing exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare proposed fees and profit margins to fees charged by affiliated markets and other exchanges (e.g., Nasdaq, NYSE American) to demonstrate comparability or competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example comparisons: 10Gb ULL proposed fee lower than Nasdaq and much lower than NYSE American; consider combined profit margin across affiliated markets (e.g., 9.5% overall for 10Gb ULL across affiliates) when presenting reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness not solely based on projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Projections and cost analyses should not be the sole basis for determining whether a fee is reasonable; information should confirm the exchange is not seeking supra-competitive profits but also consider value of service and competitive context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use projections as one input among others (cost basis, comparative pricing, service value) and state that estimates alone should not determine permissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable allocation / not unfairly discriminatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees must be reasonable, fair, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory — designed to align fees with services provided and applied equally to all subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify distinctions (e.g., higher fees for 10Gb ULL users) by demonstrable differences in usage/resource consumption (10Gb users account for >99% of message traffic), and show that fee differences reflect the relative consumption of shared resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform flat-fee treatment and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the same flat fee uniformly to all market participants who purchase additional Limited Service MEI Ports; all Market Makers eligible for four free ports and any purchases beyond are subject to the same monthly rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the structure applies equally and does not favor categories of market participants; cite prior filings with similar structures that were not suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-market competition / burden-on-competition assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the proposed fees impose any burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the Act (e.g., whether fees disadvantage certain participants or impose barriers to entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss whether fees are uniform across participants, whether pricing is associated with relative usage, whether third-party connectivity providers preserve affordability for smaller firms, and whether proposed pricing could lead to reduced/discontinued use by some participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-market competition / broader competitive effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the proposed fee change will impose any burden on inter-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the Act (e.g., whether fee increases render the exchange more or less competitive relative to peers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider that a substantial fee increase could make it easier for other exchanges to compete; conversely, fee increases are not predatory unless they constitute anti-competitive conduct. Use comparative pricing to show competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of historical losses and business strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Take into account the exchange's prior strategic choices (e.g., offering low-cost connectivity to attract order flow) and cumulative net losses when evaluating the reasonableness of raising fees to upgrade technology and absorb increased costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why prior below-market pricing was used (to attract participants) and why current fee increases are needed to achieve sustainable operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of shared-costs across affiliated markets
rubrics_metrics.description: When sharing costs across multiple affiliated exchanges, account for efficiencies and synergies that lower allocated costs per exchange; note that single-exchange operators allocate costs differently which affects profit margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise that Commission Staff should consider different allocation methodologies (across multiple markets vs single market) and apply determinations consistently; recognize that cost-sharing can legitimately result in different profit margins for comparable fee levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of costs to be covered by connectivity/port fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and justify cost categories recovered by connectivity/port fees, including hardware, software, human capital, network monitoring/support, storage, surveillance, security appliances, network switching infrastructure, and depreciation of equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how these costs enable measurement of network performance (e.g., nanosecond granularity), improvements to performance, and the provision of service level expectations to subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource-consumption correlation (message/connection-driven costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that as message volume or number of connections increases, correlated costs (storage, surveillance, service expenses) also increase and should be considered when allocating costs among users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use message traffic statistics and connection counts to justify differential charging (e.g., 10Gb users consume majority of messages and therefore bear larger share of related costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to commenter requests and scope of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Address commenter requests for additional data and information; resist requests that would require opaque or moving-target disclosures materially over and above that provided by competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that issues of broad disclosure should be addressed through Commission rulemaking rather than resolved ad hoc in individual filings; explain what additional disclosure is germane vs. what is overbroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and submission procedures for public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear instructions for submitting comments to the Commission: electronic comment form or email to rule-comments@sec.gov (include file number SR-EMERALD-2023-27 on subject), or paper comments in triplicate to the SEC Secretary; note that the Commission will post comments on its website and make filings available in the Public Reference Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request that commenters use one method only to help processing; include file number on submissions and explain where submitted materials will be posted and inspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule change effectiveness and Commission action/timing
rubrics_metrics.description: State effective date under section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) and Rule 19b-4(f)(2), and describe that Commission may suspend the change within 60 days and institute proceedings to determine approval or disapproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform readers of the procedural timeline and the Commission's authority to act within the statutory window for summary suspension and subsequent proceedings.
